content: The National Standards for Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support (DSMES), as outlined by the American Diabetes Association (ADA), emphasize a comprehensive approach to patient care. This approach integrates clinical education, behavioral support, and psychosocial engagement to holistically address the needs of individuals managing diabetes. With the increasing availability of digital health tools, DSMES programs have expanded their reach through online platforms. This development allows these resources to become accessible to a broader population, particularly benefiting individuals who may have previously faced barriers related to geographic location or limited mobility. To address the challenges posed by the digital divide, DSMES programs have been adapted to ensure equitable access for patients with limited technological resources. These adaptations include strategies to provide digital tools and support to underserved communities, ensuring that all individuals, regardless of their access to technology, can benefit from these educational and supportive services.
